newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs outlook nervous after Easter slide.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs outlook nervous after Easter slide.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds ended lower in pre-holiday trade on Friday and dealers said prices could be marked down more when the market reopens on Tuesday.
"The feeling is we are in a down trend. A lot of people are unsettled by what is happening in the U.S. and we could open lower again on Tuesday," one trader said.

By the close of a shortened session, the benchmark 10-year OLO yield had risen to 6.05 percent from 6.00 percent late on Thursday despite annual coupon payments on Friday of around 60 billion Belgian francs. Dealers said insurance companies, the main beneficiaries, were waiting before reinvesting the cash.
One trader said that Tuesday's tone could be set by European markets' reaction to final U.S. fourth quarter growth data due at 1330 GMT on Friday. GDP is seen up 4.00 percent.

However, room for any gains would be limited, they noted, because the German market, which was closed today, would have to adjust in any case to Thursday's pre-Easter slide in U.S. Treasuries. Trade next week will also be dominated by the spectre of Friday's March non-farm payrolls in the U.S., they noted.
"People cannot hold on to their cash for too long, but I don't know where the support will come," one trader said.
